description: Imports a single LinkedIn organization page's profile, follower statistics, share statistics, and total follower count from the LinkedIn v2 REST API.

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment: the API version `v2` is baked into `url_base`. No `X-Restli-Protocol-Version` header and no `LinkedIn-Version` header is sent by this connector (the sibling source-linkedin-ads-v2 does send `X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0`; this one does not).

configFields.name: credentials.auth_method
configFields.description: Discriminator: "oAuth2.0" or "access_token". Absent means legacy top-level access_token config.

configFields.name: credentials.access_token

authTierRationale: Two alternative credential modes are offered. The 'Access token' mode requires exactly one secret (credentials.access_token) pasted into the config and is sent as a plain bearer token, so by the field-shape definition it is T1_SIMPLE — with the honest caveat that LinkedIn only issues such a token through its Developers OAuth Token Tools, which in practice requires the user to already own a LinkedIn developer app with Community Management products approved, and the token expires in ~2 months (per the in-code comment), so it is operationally closer to T2 and needs manual rotation. The 'OAuth2.0' mode is unambiguously T3_BYO_REFRESH: the user supplies client_id, client_secret AND refresh_token, and the connector performs a refresh_token grant against https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken. Estuary's hosted control plane can shortcut this: __main__.py registers a flow.OAuth2Spec with provider 'linkedin' and authorization_code templates, so in the hosted UI the user just clicks through consent — but standalone, without that control plane, the OAuth mode is T3. authTierOverall reports the easiest offered mode.

unionMisfits.description: This connector does not use the CDK's request_params hook at all. Query strings are urlencoded and concatenated onto the value returned by path() (e.g. base_path 'organizationalEntityFollowerStatistics?' + urlencode({...})). I have split them back into `path` + `params` for the schema, which is semantically faithful but does not mirror the code's structure; a reader diffing against the source will find no params dict.

Neither 'merge', 'append', nor 'snapshot_with_tombstone' cleanly fits. The shim synthesizes the key /_meta/row_id from a per-binding counter (ResourceState.rowId) that is monotonic across the whole task lifetime and never reset between refreshes, and emits op='u' with no deletion of prior rows. Practically that behaves like append (each refresh lands at fresh row_ids), but the intent of a full_refresh binding is a snapshot. There is no tombstone emission anywhere in the shim.

proposedShape.keySource: connector-synthesized monotonic counter, not source data

unionMisfits.description: organization_lookup and total_follower_count return a single JSON object which parse_response wraps as one record ([response.json()]) — a one-document 'stream'. There is no records envelope, so recordsPath is null; that null means 'the whole body is the record', not 'unknown'.

abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No headers are set anywhere in this connector. request_headers is never overridden and no X-Restli-Protocol-Version / LinkedIn-Version header is added, unlike the sibling source-linkedin-ads-v2. Whatever the airbyte-cdk HttpStream and the authenticator add is all that is sent; I did not read the pinned airbyte-cdk (^0.52) source, which is outside the provided tree.
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.prefix: TokenAuthenticator is imported from airbyte_cdk.sources.streams.http.auth and constructed with only token=..., so the prefix is the CDK default. The airbyte-cdk package is not in the provided tree, so I did not verify the default is 'Bearer' from source (it is bearer by strong convention, hence type 'bearer' with medium confidence).
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: Nothing in the connector or in shim_airbyte_cdk.py declares an interval, cron, or Go-duration schedule. Cadence is entirely decided by the Flow runtime outside this code.
abstained.execution.continuity: mode is 'poll' over a stateless REST API; continuity is optional for poll mode and no server-side artifact of any kind is created (no slot, cursor registration, or scratch object). Nothing accrues on LinkedIn's side if we stop.
abstained.streams[].cursorField: All four streams are full_refresh only. LinkedinPagesStream never sets cursor_field, get_updated_state, or an incremental param; discover emits no cursorField. There is genuinely no cursor.
abstained.streams[].schedules: No per-binding schedule exists in the resource config schema (stream/syncMode/namespace/cursorField only).
abstained.streams[].pull.backfill / incremental: There is no historical/ongoing split — one unparameterized GET returns the current state each run, so only `snapshot` is populated.
abstained.rateLimits: The code only logs a message on HTTP 429 saying LinkedIn limits reset at midnight UTC; no numeric quota, no backoff_time override, and no page-size control exist in this connector, so I record no concrete rate-limit figure.
